style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The dawn psalm of the thirsty soul, written in the wilderness of Judah -- David a fugitive again, likely from Absalom, praying in the same badlands where his greater Son would later fast forty days. The desert supplies the psalm's whole vocabulary: a soul that thirsts, flesh that faints, a dry and weary land with no water -- and David reads his geography as a parable of his deepest need, which is not water but God. The psalm's famous valuation stands at its center: Your covenant love is better than life itself -- the one comparison that reorders every other price a man pays. From that valuation flows a whole liturgy for hard places: hands lifted in His name, the soul satisfied as at a feast of rich food while standing in a desert, memory working through the night watches, joy sung in the shadow of His wings. Verse 8 gives the psalm's physics in one line: my soul clings hard after You -- and Your right hand is what holds me up; the pursuit from below is sustained by the grip from above. The enemies who hunt his life will go down to the depths and the jackals, but the king will rejoice in God -- and every mouth that swears by Him will glory when the lying mouths are stopped.

1.text: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God; at first light I seek You. My soul thirsts for You, my flesh faints with longing for You, in a dry and weary land where there is no water.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David, when he was in the wilderness [midbar] of Judah [Yehudah]. O God [Elohim], You are my God [El]; early will I seek [shachar -- seek at dawn, seek diligently] You: my soul [nephesh] thirsts [tsame] for You, my flesh [basar] longs [kamah -- faints with longing] for You in a dry [tsiyyah] and thirsty ['weary', ayeph, the KJV margin] land [eretz], where no water [mayim] is;
1.notes: shachar (H7836) is dawn-seeking, built on the word for daybreak: God sought before anything else gets the day. tsame (H6770) and kamah (H3642) run the thirst through soul AND basar -- the whole man dehydrated for God. The midbar (H4057) of Judah is real geography turned diagnosis: the land without mayim is a portrait of life without Him.

2.text: So I have gazed on You in the sanctuary, beholding Your power and Your glory.
2.amp: To see [raah] Your power [oz] and Your glory [kabod], so as I have seen [chazah -- gazed on, as a seer] You in the sanctuary [qodesh].
2.notes: The desert thirst runs on sanctuary memory: chazah (H2372), the seer's beholding of Psalm 27:4, files away oz and kabod (H5797, H3519) for the day the qodesh is out of reach. What worship banks, exile withdraws.

3.text: Because Your covenant love is better than life itself, my lips will praise You.
3.amp: Because Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] is better [tov] than life [chay], my lips [saphah] shall praise [shabach -- laud, commend] You.
3.notes: The psalm's summit and one of Scripture's greatest sentences: chesed (H2617) weighed against chay (H2416) -- against life, the thing men trade everything to keep -- and chesed wins. A man who believes this verse is unblackmailable; the worst threat has lost its leverage (cf. Acts 20:24).

4.text: So I will bless You while I have life; in Your name I will lift my hands.
4.amp: Thus will I bless [barak] You while I live [chay]: I will lift up [nasa] my hands [kaph] in Your name [shem].
4.notes: The valuation of verse 3 becomes a life-term commitment: barak (H1288) for the duration of the chay that chesed outranks. The lifted kaph (H3709) is prayer's oldest posture -- open palms raised in the shem, empty hands showing exactly what they came to receive.

5.text: My soul will be satisfied as with marrow and rich abundance, and my mouth will praise You with lips full of ringing joy,
5.amp: My soul [nephesh] shall be satisfied [saba] as with marrow ['fatness', chelev, the KJV margin] and fatness [deshen -- rich abundance]; and my mouth [peh] shall praise [halal] You with joyful [renanah] lips [saphah]:
5.notes: Feast language spoken in a desert: saba (H7646), satisfaction, measured in chelev and deshen (H2459, H1880) -- the choicest portions of a sacrifice-banquet -- while the man himself stands in the waterless midbar. God satisfies at a table circumstances never set (cf. Psalm 23:5).

6.text: when I remember You upon my bed and meditate on You through the watches of the night.
6.amp: When I remember [zakar] You upon my bed [yatsua], and meditate [hagah -- murmur, muse] on You in the night watches [ashmurah].
6.notes: The fugitive's insomnia converted: zakar (H2142) and hagah (H1897) -- Psalm 1's chewing meditation -- working through the ashmurot (H821), watch by watch. The bed that anxiety would keep awake, worship keeps awake instead; same sleeplessness, opposite occupation (cf. Psalm 119:148).

7.text: For You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings I sing out for joy.
7.amp: Because You have been my help [ezrah], therefore in the shadow [tsel] of Your wings [kanaph] will I rejoice [ranan -- ring out with joy].
7.notes: The logic of remembered rescue: 'You HAVE been' funds 'I WILL rejoice.' The tsel kanaph (H6738, H3671), the wing-shadow of Psalm 91:4 and Ruth 2:12 -- and the singing happens IN the shadow, in the dark place itself, not after leaving it.

8.text: My soul clings hard after You; Your right hand keeps its hold and holds me upright.
8.amp: My soul [nephesh] follows hard [dabaq -- clings fast] after [achar] You: Your right hand [yamin] upholds [tamak -- grips, supports] me.
8.notes: The psalm's physics in one verse: dabaq (H1692), the covenant cleaving-verb of Ruth 1:14, aimed at God -- and beneath the clinging, tamak (H8551), His yamin (H3225) doing the actual load-bearing. The soul pursues; the hand sustains the pursuit. Perseverance is grip inside Grip (cf. Philippians 3:12).

9.text: But those who seek my life to destroy it will go down into the depths of the earth.
9.amp: But those that seek [baqash] my soul [nephesh], to destroy [sho -- devastate] it, shall go [bo] into the lower parts [tachti] of the earth [eretz].
9.notes: Two seekings frame the psalm: David baqash (H1245) God at dawn; the enemies baqash his nephesh for ruin. Their trajectory answers their aim -- down, to the tachti eretz (H8482), the depths that swallow what the grave claims.

10.text: They will be poured out to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for the jackals.
10.amp: They shall fall ['be made to run out like water by the hands of', nagar, the KJV margin] by the sword [cherev]: they shall be a portion [menah] for foxes [shual -- jackals].
10.notes: The margin preserves the grim verb: nagar, poured out like water -- the hunters spilled by the cherev (H2719) they drew. menah (H4521), the portion-word of feasts, served instead to the shualim (H7776), the battlefield's jackals: the portion-seekers become a portion.

11.text: But the king will rejoice in God; everyone who swears by Him will glory, when the mouth of those who speak lies is stopped and sealed.
11.amp: But the king [melek] shall rejoice [samach] in God [Elohim]; every one that swears [shaba] by Him shall glory [halal]: but the mouth [peh] of them that speak [dabar] lies [sheqer] shall be stopped [sakar -- shut up, sealed].
11.notes: David speaks of himself in the third person -- the melek (H4428) whose crown is in exile but whose joy is not. Those who shaba (H7650) by God, whose allegiance is sworn to Him, inherit the halal; the peh sheqer (H8267), the lying mouth that fueled the rebellion, gets sakar (H5534), sealed. Truth outlasts the propaganda; the king outlasts the coup.
